title: Precision Ad Targeting on a $500 Budget
excerpt: Run high-ROI campaigns on Facebook, Google, and Reddit with a sub-$500 budget. Covers audience selection, creative testing, and bidding strategy with real CPA data.
content:
## Why Small Budgets Outperform

Accounts spending $500-$1,000/month achieve lower CPA ($24.38) than accounts spending $5,000-$10,000 ($32.17 CPA). Small budgets demand tight targeting and ruthless testing. A $500 budget reaches active Facebook status in just 2 days, minimizing learning-phase waste.

## Facebook Hyper-Niche Targeting

Layer three criteria: specific interest, job title, and behavior. This drops CPA by 56%. Run 3 ad variants: static image with statistic, short video, and carousel. A/B test 3 headlines and 2 CTAs to improve CTR by 40%.

## Google Long-Tail Strategy

Target competitor-branded keywords with an alternative angle. CPC drops to $0.30-$0.80 versus $3-$8. Convert at 4-6%. Allocate $350 to Search and $150 to remarketing from a $500 budget.

## Reddit: The Underpriced Channel

Reddit Ads offer $6-$12 CPA in niche subreddits. Subreddit-level targeting delivers 3-5x lower CPA than Facebook. Use native-looking text-and-image posts. Budget $5-$10/day for 30 days.

## The Optimization Loop

Test 3 creatives at $15/day for 3 days. Kill ads above target CPA. Double budget on winner. Repeat weekly. This improved ROAS from 1.8x to 4.7x. On $500/month, that is $2,350 revenue.
